name: Cryomere-Vault
description: Cryomere-Vault is a giant among ice worlds, wrapped in a dense nitrogen-methane haze that gives the planet a soft, amber-tinged glow when seen from orbit. Below the haze, storm bands the size of continents circle the globe without end, driving blizzards of methane snow across frozen lake plains that stretch beyond sight. A thin ring of ice debris—shattered moonlet, most likely—slices across the sky like a scar of white fire.

Standing on the surface is less like standing on a world and more like standing inside weather. The dense atmosphere carries sound strangely: storms arrive as a rising sub-bass hum felt through the boots minutes before any visible cloud. Daylight never fully arrives; even at noon the sun is a smeared bright patch behind the haze, and the landscape glows rather than shines.

Nothing lives here and nothing ever has—the cold is too absolute for chemistry to bother. Yet the system's early colonists saw value in that sterility, and they built the vault: a fortified research station in high orbit from which, according to fragmentary logs, they studied 'containment under natural cryostasis.' The station went dark seventy years ago after a single garbled distress transmission. Its docking arms still stand open, its reactor still ticking on standby, as though it expects ships to arrive.

Helium-3 skimmers work Cryomere-Vault's upper atmosphere in growing numbers, drawn by fuel prices and the planet's indifference to being harvested. But boarding parties that dock with the derelict vault report sealed interior bulkheads arranged from the inside, and cargo manifests listing mass that no longer matches what sensors weigh. The station's log core has never been recovered. The company that owns the claim would very much like to know why.
